And he answered [ ... ]: {a.1} "This religion that I have chosen is superior and (5) better than the other, earlier religions in ten things.
First, that the religions of the forerunners was in one land and one language. Then my religion (10) was *able to be revealed in every land and in all languages and be taught in distant lands.
{a.2} Second, that the previous religions <persisted> as long as long as there were pure leaders in them. And when the leaders were raised up (to Paradise), (15) then their religion was changed and they became slack in commandments and deeds. And they were deceived through [I/V] greed, fire, and [lust]. But my [religion] will stand firm and through living teachers, (5) bishops, elects, and hearers and through its wisdom and deeds it will endure until the very end.
{a.3} Third, that the previous souls, whose deeds were not fulfilled in (10) their own religion come to my religion and it will be itself the door to their release.

The third, the blessed places without count and number in which the (5) light gods, angels, mahraspands, and pow- ers dwell, in great bliss and joy. (10) The Fourth, the pure air in the light paradise, wondrous, beautiful to behold: immea- surable (is) its goodness for them. By supernatural power it shall by itself bring into being the god's marvelous (15) dress and garment, throne, diadem, and fragrant wreath, ornaments, and fineries of all sorts. The fifth, the light earth, *self-existent, eternal, (20) miraculous. In *height it is beyond *reach, its *depth cannot be perceived. No enemy and no *injurer walk this earth. Its (25) divine pavement is of the substance of diamond that does not shake forever. All good things are born from it: adorned, graceful hills wholly covered with flowers, grown (30) in much excellence; green fruit-bearing trees whose fruits never *drop, never rot, and never become wormed; [V] springs flowing with ambro- sia (35) that fill the whole paradise; its groves and plans; countless mansions and palaces, thrones and *benches that exist in perpetuity for ever and ever. (40) Thus arranged is the paradise in these five greatnesses. They are calm in quietude and know no fear. {ac.2} But that power of the light that is so mixed with darkness that it cannot be separated from it again, which is not (20) of the same form because from the begin- ning it foresaw, "So it is for me, because it was so decided." Therefore it is not called of the same form.

(25) {ac.3} And again, those five (sons of First Man) prayed in the battle to Ohrm- ezdbag (First Man), "Do not leave us in the corpse of darkness, but send us (30) power and a helper!" And Ohrmezdbag promised them, "I will not abandon you to the pow- ers of darkness." In that case it was not (35) the power that knew, "For me the mixing with darkness in the beginning reaches an injury and heaviness [R/ii] so wretched that I cannot be taken away and (40) separated from darkness." No, that was the power that knew, "My mixture is of such a kind that I can be purified and saved by the help of Ohrmezdbag (45) and the brothers."

{ac.4} And they did not pray for that reason that, if they did not pray, then (50) Ohrmezdbag would not help them. But to them on account of that prayer.
